reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: In src/position.rs, table owns an ecalloc POSITION array, table_size records capacity and table_rows the initialized geometry; pos_shift temporarily owns a converted line buffer.
owner_creation.invariant: Capacity and initialized row bounds describe different extents.

aliases_escapes.analysis: In src/position.rs, most access is through raw global table cursors; get_scrpos returns copied coordinates, while callers can enter cleanup using the same globals during allocation failure.
aliases_escapes.invariant: Copies of positions do not make the backing table live.

callback_targets.analysis: In src/position.rs, there are direct input/conversion/display calls and no stored callback; ecalloc may call out_of_memory then quit, indirectly reentering position readers.
callback_targets.invariant: Allocation is a possible cleanup reentry point.

invalidation.analysis: In src/position.rs, shrink/regrow explicitly invalidates changed rows and query bounds use min(sc_height,table_rows); growth still frees table before replacing its published pointer.
invalidation.invariant: Geometry checks cannot validate a freed table pointer.

mutation_commit.analysis: The ownership state described by src/position.rs remains published while pos_init frees the old array at line 184 without clearing table before the RHS ecalloc call. The assignment at 188 occurs only after ecalloc returns. Failure therefore leaves table pointing at freed memory, with the previous capacity/row metadata still published (M0-MEM-004).
mutation_commit.invariant: Replacement is not a failure-preserving owner transaction.

release_pair.analysis: In src/position.rs, growth pairs old allocation with free and pos_shift frees cline; table remains process-owned at exit, but the old global address is stale during replacement.
release_pair.invariant: A freed allocation must not remain a readable global owner.

error_cleanup.analysis: For src/position.rs, replacement allocation failure calls ecalloc -> out_of_memory -> quit -> edit(NULL) -> edit_ifile(NULL) -> close_file. With a current file and is_tty, close_file calls get_scrpos; nonnull table and available rows >=2 allow a read of the freed array (M0-MEM-004).
error_cleanup.invariant: Fatal growth cleanup can revisit the old table alias.

signals_handoff.analysis: In src/position.rs, direct handler termination can also enter cleanup; bounds tests cover ordinary small/shrink/growth geometry but do not approve reentry during failed replacement.
signals_handoff.invariant: Existing position and raw-owner findings remain recorded.
limitations: Source-level growth/fatal-cleanup ordering concern is recorded under existing M0-MEM-001; no new runtime proof or fix is claimed. M0-MEM-003 and IND-POS-F4 remain open.

src/pager.rs.relationship: The allocator and quit path can enter fatal cleanup while the reviewed owner is partly replaced. Target: FILE:src/position.rs.

src/edit.rs.relationship: File activation/close reads position state or resets input status, establishing the reviewed cross-file lifecycle dependency. Target: FILE:src/position.rs.

src/signal.rs.relationship: Handlers may enter output, filter/queue mutation or cleanup while the reviewed ordinary owner has live aliases. Target: FILE:src/position.rs.
